reproFailure: Before the fix, 27 new or changed tests failed: a manifest blocker naming an unrelated ticket was commented on and exited 0 on both trackers (expected a refusal or a listed note), a manifest URL was written into the ledger row, a cross-repository head settled (exit 0), a manifest ledger other than the operator's was accepted, a passing lift could drop another test's row, and a 70,000-character title produced a 70,290-character note. After independent review, 12 more failed at 34f79813: a tag named after the default branch replaced the trust source on both trackers, a tag named after the head replaced it, a head name acted as a git option, a head equal to the default branch was pushed to, a trial-branch hook ran under a relative core.hooksPath, a repeated lift was told repeatedly, failing lifts with empty, missing or malformed blockers were not refused, and the verdict report printed manifest strings raw.
assumptions: The trusted source is the tip of refs/heads/<default branch> fetched from origin into a ref of the process's own, read in a throwaway worktree; the trial branch, manifest.base, the PR base, local state and tags are not trusted.
The default branch's name comes from gh's resolved repository while the fetch is from origin, so in an upstream-and-fork clone the trust source can be the operator's fork. Declared, not fixed.
The trusted ledger path is the operator's --ledger or the default .canary/quarantine.json; manifest.ledger must equal it.

jira_projects and quarantine tags come from whatever is checked out, or the operator's flags. An operator running from the trial branch lets its editor set the Jira allow-list and which bare keys count as tickets. Declared, not fixed.

A blocker is direct only when its id is a ticket the trusted row names under the audit's own first-source rule; the manifest's claim plays no part. A claimed chain only moves a target from refused to listed.
Only pass and fail outcomes act on the ledger, so rows are checked for those; flaky and missing lifts are not checked against the ledger.

The run's results are editor-influenced because the run executes the editor's branch. Whether a failing lift must be proven part of the trial was not decided, so a failing lift for a real row can tell the ticket that row names, including an open one, with a note saying its blocker was read as resolved.

A real trial cannot produce a failing lift with no blocker: selectRows takes candidates and abstained rows that carry a marker line, and those always have at least one blocker. So that shape is refused.
A relative core.hooksPath is refused rather than overridden, read from the operator's repository before any worktree exists. This affects suites using a relative hooks path such as husky's default.
A trial opened before via was recorded is refused if a failing blocker was handed off; trials are short-lived, and opening a new one recovers.
A trial against another branch is refused if its row exists only there; the row must reach the default branch first.
